title: Why Your Drains Gurgle: Understanding Airflow Restrictions
description: Gurgling noises coming from sink or shower drains often indicate a atmospheric venting problem within the drainage system. When water flows down a drain pipe, it displaces air ahead of it and creates a vacuum behind it. If the plumbing vent stack is blocked or improperly sized, the draining water pulls air from the nearest available source—often sucking water out of nearby P-traps. This negative pressure causes the distinct gurgling sound and can break the water trap seal, allowing unpleasant sewer gases to enter living spaces. Proper venting balances atmospheric pressure throughout the drain line.
